slides.say: A cylinder is inscribed in a box. The box has a square base with side two k, and its height is five k. The cylinder has the same height, and its circles are inscribed in the squares. What fraction of the box is outside the cylinder?
at: A cylinder is inscribed in a box

slides.say: Inscribed means the cylinder fits exactly inside the box. We met inscribed shapes in circles, and here it's the same idea in three dimensions. We'll solve it in three different ways.
Let's start with the math way. The box is straight, so its volume is the base times the height. The base is two k times two k, four k squared. Times five k, that's twenty k to the power of three.
The cylinder is straight too, but we need its radius, written with k. The circle sits exactly inside the square. So the side of the square is the diameter of the circle. Two r is two k, so r is k.
at: the side of the square is the diameter

slides.say: So the cylinder is pi times k squared, times five k. That's five pi k to the power of three.
The part outside is the box minus the cylinder. To get a fraction of the box, we divide it by the box.
at: we divide it by the box

slides.say: k to the power of three cancels, and five over twenty is one over four. So it's one minus pi over four. Choice number four, but it was long.
Now let's plug in numbers, like with inscribed shapes in circles. Usually we'd think one is the easiest number.
But look at the choices. With k equal to one, choice numbers one, three and four all become one minus pi over four. One can't tell them apart.
So let's take another easy number, k is two. Then the box is four by four by ten, one hundred sixty.
The radius is half the side, two. So the cylinder is pi times two squared, times ten, forty pi.
at: The radius is half the side

slides.say: The part outside, divided by the box, is one hundred sixty minus forty pi, over one hundred sixty. That's one minus pi over four.

Now we put k equal to two into the choices. Choice number one gives one minus two pi over four, that's one minus pi over two. Choice number three gives one minus pi over eight. Choice number two is one minus pi over two. None of them is one minus pi over four.
at: Choice number two is one minus
Choice number two is one minus

slides.say: And a third way, with an estimate. Remember the rule from circles. If we make the whole shape bigger or smaller, the ratio between its parts stays the same.
So the fraction of the box outside the cylinder is the same for any k. The answer can't have k in it. So choice numbers one and three are out.
at: The answer can't have k in it
So choice numbers one and three

slides.say: Choice number two is one minus pi over two. Pi is more than three, so pi over two is more than one and a half, more than one.
One minus something bigger than one is negative. A part of the box can't be a negative fraction, so choice number two is out.
at: so choice number two is out

slides.say: And choice number four makes sense. Pi over four is a bit more than three quarters. So the cylinder fills a bit more than three quarters of the box, and a bit less than a quarter is outside. Choice number four is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number four is our answer
